body:
Chief: THE REMAINING 35 SWEEP SITES ARE SCOPED, recorded as a note on the parent bead rather than as four more open beads. I complained an hour ago about a P1 queue growing faster than three actors can drain it; opening slice beads nobody is working would be me doing exactly that. Cut each one when someone is ready to take it - the scoping is done, so that costs nothing.

Slice 2 is core, seven types, and it goes second on purpose: core is the foundation everything depends on, so its reference scope is the whole build and it is the slice most likely to surface cross-module breakage. Slice 3 is the align remainder plus features plus embed-grakern - and note Coverage in there, which is the support carrier ADR 0003 leans on, so forging one forges the support figure attached to every estimate that carries it. Slice 4 is view, thirteen types, and its reference scope INCLUDES STORYATLAS4S, so the sibling-seam rule applies: compile and run its suite. Slice 5 is document, interview and acquire.

AND I HAVE WRITTEN THE CORRECTED RANKING PRINCIPLE ONTO THE BEAD, because the mistake I made an hour ago will otherwise repeat in every slice: RANK BY WHAT THE TYPE GUARDS, NOT BY WHETHER IT VALIDATES ITSELF. My original heuristic scored each type by whether its companion held a smart constructor returning Either or Option. That is blind to a type whose guarantee is enforced somewhere else - which is exactly how AuthorizedRemoteRequest ended up ranked below four arithmetic types. Before ordering any slice, grep for who CONSTRUCTS the type, not only what its companion contains. Authorisation and privacy first, identity second, estimand carriers third, arithmetic fourth.
